prompt:
Panoramic cinematic dark-fantasy digital illustration, banner composition, 21:9. Joyful, funny, high-energy dance battle, not violence, no weapons. High contrast, sharp detail on wet neoprene, nylon webbing, octopus skin, kelp and calcium shell. Palette: obsidian black and slate grey shadows, deep Puget Sound teal and sea-glass green, neon magenta-violet stage light, warm sodium-orange emergency light from below. Dynamic triangular composition sweeping left to right with clear foreground, midground and background depth.
Setting: the Seattle waterfront at Pier 59 has collapsed into a flooded underground dance floor. Black basalt arches, shattered aquarium glass, rusted pier pilings, shallow tide-pool water glowing teal. Long ropes of bull kelp with round floating bulbs hang from the broken ceiling like streamers. A meadow of thin green eelgrass ribbons sways in the shallow water. Bright green sea lettuce on the rocks. Red-green pickleweed and tall Lyngby's sedge along the waterline. Through a breach high in the background: a grey rainy sky, a Pacific madrone tree with peeling red bark on a bluff, wild pink Nootka roses, the silhouette of the Space Needle and container cranes.
Center-left foreground, main focal point: Cordula, an athletic woman in her early thirties with a confident grin and dark hair tied back, wearing a high-visibility orange and black drysuit, a float vest, neoprene boots and a military MOLLE load frame on her back. She hits a sharp, powerful dance pose, one knee bent, one arm thrown high, holding a matte black kayak paddle with smooth rounded blunt blades overhead like a dance prop. Stuck to her forearm guard by its suction disc, like a small round buckler, is Chonks, a tiny round green spiny lumpsucker fish covered in bumpy tubercles, with big black eyes and an intense stare.
Riding on her back inside a clear water-filled backpack tank mounted on the MOLLE frame, with clear tubing and two small pumps: Barnaby, a large reddish-orange Giant Pacific Octopus, the party leader, with a slim brass collar around his mantle. His skin flashes crimson and white patterns in time with the beat, and four of his arms reach out of the tank top in elegant choreographed poses, mirroring Cordula.
Center-right midground, the opponents, both soaking wet and trying very hard: a middle-aged accountant in a grey suit and loosened tie doing a stiff robot dance while clutching a calculator, a trail of printed spreadsheet paper fluttering around them; and a young investment banker in a quarter-zip fleece vest over a dress shirt, mid-spin, slipping on the wet floor, sunglasses flying off. Both look outclassed and startled.
Right foreground: Shelly, a big oblong pale geoduck clam shell half buried in the sand, a short stubby wrinkled siphon puffing a soft cloud of sea mist across the floor like a stage fog machine.
Subtle semi-transparent glowing violet interface boxes float in the air near the top corners, blank, with no writing. Keep the upper corners darker and calmer for overlays. No text, no letters, no numbers, no words, no logos, no watermark, no signature.
